newsitem.title: USA: Glenayre shares down on U.S. paging outlook.
newsitem.headline: Glenayre shares down on U.S. paging outlook.

text.p: Glenayre Technologies Inc shares slid sharply on Thursday after the company said it expected flat growth in the U.S paging industry's network in 1997, analysts said.

"The capital expenditures from the customers have not been as rampant as 1995 and they are predicting that the expansion for 1997 is going to be in line with 1996," said Christopher Larsen, an analyst at NatWest Securities.
Glenayre shares were off four at 15-5/8 in midday trading.

The industry outlook from Glenayre, which provides equipment to the wireless telecommunications industry, coupled with recent bad news from some paging companies, has spooked Wall Street, analysts said.
"People are analyzing whether or not Glenayre is still a high-growth story," said Andrew Wiener, an analyst at Burnham Securities. "The street has lost a great deal of confidence."

Wiener said he was expecting the fiscal year 1997 earnings to be about $1.20 per share which would mean almost flat growth over three years. The First Call consensus estimate for 1997 is $1.41 per share.
